<section class="project-section" id="overview" aria-labelledby="overview-title"><div class="project-inner project-reading">
<h2 id="overview-title">A heart in four dimensions</h2>
<p class="project-lead">A cardiac cine MRI records anatomy through both space and time. Generating convincing individual slices is only part of the task: those slices also need to form a coherent, moving heart.</p>
<p>CardioDiT models complete 3D+t volumes jointly in a compact latent space. The preprint compares this approach with slice-wise 2D+t and channel-merged 3D+t models, examining image distributions, through-plane consistency, and cardiac function.</p>
</div></section>

<section class="project-section project-section--tinted" id="method" aria-labelledby="method-title"><div class="project-inner">
<h2 id="method-title">From slices to a joint 4D representation</h2>
<figure class="project-framework"><a href="../../assets/paper-figures/cardiodit-figure-1-framework.jpg"><img src="../../assets/paper-figures/cardiodit-figure-1-framework.jpg" width="1358" height="930" loading="lazy" alt="CardioDiT pipeline: encode 2D plus time slices, stack their latents into a full 4D volume, jointly denoise with a diffusion transformer, then decode."></a><figcaption>The CardioDiT framework. Figure 1 from the <a href="https://arxiv.org/html/2603.25194v1#S2.F1">preprint</a>. Select the diagram to enlarge it.</figcaption></figure>
<div class="method-steps">
<div><h3>Encode</h3><p>A spatiotemporal autoencoder compresses 2D+t slices. Their latent representations are stacked along depth.</p></div>
<div><h3>Model jointly</h3><p>A diffusion transformer processes 4D patches with positional information for all four axes.</p></div>
<div><h3>Decode</h3><p>The generated latent volume is decoded into a complete cine MRI sequence.</p></div>
</div>
</div></section>

<section class="project-section" id="results" aria-labelledby="results-title"><div class="project-inner">
<h2 id="results-title">Results from the preprint</h2>
<p class="project-reading">On the public-data evaluation, CardioDiT achieves the lowest FID and the highest precision and recall among the three compared generators.</p>
<div class="project-table-scroll" role="region" aria-label="Public dataset comparison" tabindex="0">
<table class="project-results"><caption>Public datasets: ACDC and M&amp;Ms-2 · 50 synthetic volumes per model</caption><thead><tr><th scope="col">Model</th><th scope="col">FID ↓</th><th scope="col">Precision ↑</th><th scope="col">Recall ↑</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><th scope="row">Factorized 2D+t LDM</th><td>100.1</td><td>0.89</td><td>0.17</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Channel-merged 3D+t U-Net</th><td>221.5</td><td>0.59</td><td>0.64</td></tr>
<tr class="result-highlight"><th scope="row">CardioDiT</th><td><strong>71.9</strong></td><td><strong>0.97</strong></td><td><strong>0.70</strong></td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>
<p class="project-source">Selected metrics from <a href="https://arxiv.org/html/2603.25194v1#S2.T1">Table 1</a>, using CineMA features and the real validation cohort as reference. ↓ Lower is better; ↑ higher is better. Full structural and cardiac-function analyses are in the paper.</p>
<details class="project-limitations"><summary>Scope and limitations</summary><p>The preprint studies unconditional synthesis with fixed spatial sizes and 32-frame temporal standardization. Cyclic repetition may introduce artificial periodicity. The displayed samples illustrate model outputs; they are not a substitute for the quantitative evaluation or evidence of clinical validation.</p></details>
</div></section>

<section class="project-section project-section--tinted" id="development" aria-labelledby="development-title"><div class="project-inner">
<p class="eyebrow">Beyond the preprint · Development update</p>
<h2 id="development-title">Ongoing work</h2>
<div class="development-layout"><div>
<h3>More flexible spatial and temporal modeling</h3><p>The development code adds axis-aware 4D rotary positional encoding and support for variable input shapes and native temporal lengths.</p>
<h3>Exploring alternative generative training</h3><p>Current experiments investigate flow matching and self-conditioning alongside the original diffusion approach. The example shown here is from a fixed-shape F07 run, using 4D rotary positional encoding.</p>
<p class="development-note">These are subsequent experiments, separate from the benchmark results above. Comparative quality or speed gains have not yet been established here.</p>

Central slice, quantized decoding, EMA weights. A synthetic development example from the local experiment archive.</figcaption></figure></div>
